**Abstract**

Natural language call routing can be treated as an instance of topic categorization of documents after speech recognition of calls. This categorization consists of two important parts. The first one is text preprocessing for numerical data extraction and the second one is classification with machine learning algorithms. In this paper, we investigate various text categorization methods to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of call routing in a natural language processing (NLP) context. We evaluate the performance of traditional NLP techniques such as Bag-of-Words (BoW), Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF), and advanced neural network models like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTMs). The study employs a large dataset of transcribed customer service calls to test these methods. Our findings indicate that while BoW and TF-IDF are effective for initial preprocessing and feature extraction, deep learning models offer superior classification results due to their ability to capture complex patterns in textual data. These methodologies not only improve call routing but also enhance user experience by ensuring quicker resolution of queries through more accurate categorization. The study also highlights potential challenges and provides recommendations for further improvements in text preprocessing and model tuning for real-world implementation. Overall, this research contributes significantly to the application of sophisticated text categorization methods in natural language processing tasks within customer service operations.

This study introduces "Adaptive Ensembling," an innovative UDA framework specifically designed to address the challenges of domain shift and data scarcity in political document datasets. By leveraging transfer learning and ensemble methods, our approach enhances model performance on target domains where labeled data is limited. The proposed method integrates multiple pre-trained models that are adaptively weighted based on their performance on a diverse set of auxiliary tasks, ensuring robustness and generalizability across various political document types. Empirical evaluations on several benchmark datasets from diverse political contexts demonstrate that Adaptive Ensembling achieves state-of-the-art results in both precision and recall, highlighting its potential as a powerful tool for domain-specific text analysis. These findings underscore the critical importance of context-adaptive techniques in advancing the automated processing of political documents, thereby facilitating more efficient and nuanced research into complex political phenomena.

This research contributes to the field by providing a scalable solution to the domain shift problem, enabling political scientists and data analysts to focus on meaningful document collections without manual filtering, thus fostering more effective and insightful research methodologies.

This paper presents comparisons between predicted and measured data for a live GSM system. Our propagation prediction software tool is based on 3D-ray tracing, and considers wave interactions, such as free space, reflection, diffraction, and scattering. The underlying methodology accounts for the complexities of urban environments, where obstacles like buildings and vegetation significantly affect signal propagation. This study aims to validate the accuracy and reliability of our 3D ray-tracing simulation against real-world GSM signal measurements obtained from various locations within a densely populated city environment.

To ensure comprehensive analysis, we have selected a diverse set of scenarios ranging from open fields to complex urban canyons. For each scenario, multiple measurement points were strategically chosen to cover various distances and angles relative to base stations. Signal strength was recorded at these points using portable GSM measurement devices that match the frequency bands used in our simulations.

The results indicate high correlation between predicted and measured values, demonstrating the capability of 3D ray-tracing in accurately predicting signal strengths and coverage areas even in challenging urban landscapes. Furthermore, our analysis highlights specific conditions under which discrepancies may arise, providing insights into potential improvements for future model iterations.

Our findings contribute significantly to the field of wireless network planning and optimization, offering a robust framework for engineers and researchers to enhance the design and deployment of cellular networks. By understanding the limitations and strengths of 3D ray-tracing models, network providers can make more informed decisions about infrastructure placement and adjustments necessary to improve overall service quality and reliability.

**Abstract**

Effects of a carboxylated styrene-butadiene-based liquid additive on the microstructure, mechanical strength, and decolorization resistance of an inorganic pigment layer in the color block have been examined. More dense inorganic pigment layers, characterized by lower porosity and improved interparticle bonding, were observed after the addition of the liquid additive at various concentrations (0.1 wt%, 0.5 wt%, and 1.0 wt%). The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images and mercury intrusion porosimetry (MIP) results revealed significant reductions in pore sizes and volume fractions within the pigment layers. Additionally, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) analysis indicated the presence of hydrogen bonding between the functional groups of the liquid additive and the pigment particles, which enhanced the structural stability. The mechanical strength of the pigmented layers was measured via compressive tests, showing that samples incorporating the liquid additive displayed up to 30% higher strength compared to the control group without additives. Moreover, accelerated weathering tests performed under UV light exposure demonstrated that the decolorization rate of the samples decreased by approximately 25% when the additive concentration was optimized, indicating enhanced durability against fading and color degradation. Overall, these findings suggest that the incorporation of a carboxylated styrene-butadiene-based liquid additive can significantly improve the performance characteristics of inorganic pigment layers in color blocks, making them more suitable for applications requiring high durability and stability.

GHz third harmonic superconducting cavities have been used to increase the peak bunch current and to compensate for non-linear distortions in the longitudinal phase space due to sinusoidal 1.3 GHz accelerating cavity voltage (1). The power coupler is a critical component of these cavities, responsible for efficiently transferring RF power from the waveguide system to the cavity. In this study, we present simulations and optimizations of a new power coupler designed specifically for 3.9-GHz superconducting cavities at Fermilab. Utilizing advanced electromagnetic simulation software, we explore various geometrical configurations of the coupler with the aim of minimizing ohmic losses, maximizing coupling efficiency, and ensuring long-term reliability under high-power operation conditions. We also analyze thermal and mechanical stresses, considering both quench prevention strategies and operational stability over time. Our results indicate that a novel tapered shape design, combined with optimized dielectric material placement within the coupler's aperture, significantly enhances performance metrics. Comparative analysis with existing couplers confirms the viability of our design, demonstrating superior efficiency and reduced risk of failure modes such as multipactoring. This work contributes to the ongoing effort to enhance accelerator performance at Fermilab, with potential applications in future particle physics experiments requiring higher beam intensities.

In this work, we mainly investigate the effect of PT-symmetric operations on the dynamic behavior of the relative entropy of coherence for a two-level system within non-Markovian environments and put forward a feasible physical scheme to recover coherence by utilizing optimal parameters. We first explore the fundamental properties of PT-symmetric operators under different coupling strengths between the two-level system and the environment. Through numerical simulations, we uncover a unique phase transition that occurs in the system's coherence dynamics when varying the PT-symmetry breaking parameter. Our results reveal that PT symmetry can enhance coherence in the presence of strong non-Markovian effects, providing new insights into the interplay between non-Hermitian physics and quantum information theory.

Furthermore, we demonstrate how optimal control methods can be applied to manipulate the system-environment interactions for recovering lost coherence. By carefully tuning the PT-symmetric parameters and the environmental correlations, we observe significant recovery of coherence even after severe dephasing induced by the environment. The robustness of this approach opens up potential applications in designing more resilient quantum devices under realistic noisy conditions.

Overall, our study advances the understanding of coherence dynamics in complex quantum systems and suggests novel strategies for enhancing quantum information processing capabilities.

Notably, the combination therapy using rifampicin and dapsone showed reduced lesion formation and a lower bacterial index compared to other regimens, suggesting synergistic action against resistant strains. This research underscores the necessity for rigorous preclinical evaluation of antimicrobial agents and the potential benefit of multi-drug combinations in treating leprosy cases with suspected intrinsic resistance. Further studies are warranted to confirm these findings and to explore additional drug combinations that may enhance treatment outcomes in drug-resistant leprosy.

In recent years, the increase of non-linear loads in electrical power systems has sparked significant research into power quality issues. The shunt active power filter (SAPF) is a power electronic device that has been developed to improve power quality by compensating for harmonics, reactive power, and other distortions caused by non-linear loads. This paper presents a comparative study of two high-performance current control techniques for SAPFs: Instantaneous Reactive Power Theory (IRPT) and Direct Power Control (DPC).

The IRPT method, based on the clamped model currents from the instantaneous active and reactive components, offers simplicity and real-time processing efficiency. Conversely, the DPC technique directly controls both active and reactive powers by dividing the switching states space into several regions, enabling precise and efficient tracking of the reference currents.

The study evaluates these methods using a 30 kW three-phase SAPF prototype under various loading conditions and harmonic distortion scenarios. Performance metrics such as dynamic response, steady-state accuracy, total harmonic distortion (THD), and computational complexity are analyzed.

Simulation results indicate that while both techniques effectively mitigate harmonic distortion and improve overall power quality, the DPC method demonstrates superior transient response characteristics and lower THD levels compared to IRPT. However, IRPT shows an advantage in terms of computational load, suggesting its suitability for applications where computational resources are limited.

This research provides insights for selecting the most appropriate control technique based on the specific requirements of the application, contributing to the design of more effective and efficient SAPFs. Future work will explore advanced modulation strategies to further enhance the performance of DPC and reduce the computational overhead of IRPT.
